key_insight: A multimodal graph neural network (GNN) can accurately identify and prioritize cancer immunotherapy targets, and top-ranked candidates were validated ex vivo using a clinically relevant patient-derived tumour explant platform.
problem_solved: Accelerates and improves the discovery and prioritization of immunotherapy drug targets by integrating diverse biological and clinical data and providing experimentally validated, clinically relevant candidates.
method: Integrate multimodal data (molecular profiles, protein–protein interaction networks, clinical annotations) into a graph representation of tumour biology.
Train a graph neural network to distinguish approved versus prospective targets and to score candidate targets for immunotherapy relevance.
Validate high-scoring candidates using patient-derived tumour explant assays to confirm functional and translational relevance.
impact: Demonstrates a reproducible ML→biology pipeline where multimodal GNNs produce clinically testable hypotheses, offering a template for ML practitioners to build translationally focused models with experimental validation.
visual_elements: Schematic of the multimodal GNN: nodes (genes/proteins), edges (interactions), and modality inputs (omics, clinical metadata).
Ranked-targets bar chart or precision–recall curve showing separation of approved vs prospective targets and model performance metrics.
Illustration of the patient-derived tumour explant validation workflow (sample collection → ex vivo assay → readout).
Heatmap or attention map highlighting features/paths in the graph that drove top target predictions.
paper_title: Immunotherapy drug target identification using machine learning and patient-derived tumour explant validation
paper_authors: Marcellus Augustine, Nuno Rocha Nene, Hongchang Fu, Christopher L. Pinder, Lorena Ligammari
